Subject: Retention sunlight: clarification on backup purge and evidence handoff

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call Friday. As we start scoping the DPA addendum for our retention carveouts, we need a clear operational picture from Redwood about three things before our legal team will sign: a) exact backup purge cadence for customer snapshots, b) how short-term snapshot exceptions are requested and executed, and c) the types of evidence (logs, manifests, checksums) Redwood can produce for a forensic hold.

We attached our initial matrix with questions (backup_retention_matrix.xlsx). High level ask: can you confirm whether backups for our account are maintained by Redwood-managed subprocessor(s) or a third-party backup vendor, and share the latest SLA for restore-triggered retention windows?

Two practical deadlines: our legal team needs answers by Wed 10/21 to include in the redline turnaround; procurement needs a DocuSign-ready addendum by 10/25 if possible.

Appreciate the help — looping procurement on this thread.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Data Operations Manager
Starlight Health

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: backups for Starlight are handled by Redwood-managed snapshot service (we do not currently route snapshots to a third-party backup vendor for your account); restore-triggered retention windows are configurable but default to 90 days; we can produce time-stamped manifests, snapshot checksums, and per-request audit traces for holds.

Action items I propose:
- Kimberly / Ops: confirm whether we can extend the default restore window to 180 days for Starlight as a temporary carveout during the migration (this would be a soft policy change, not storage tiering).
- Marissa: provide the runbook steps for requesting a short-term snapshot exception and an SLT (service-level timeline) for execution.

Alex — I'll also upload a short evidence sample (manifest + trace) once we have Marissa's confirm. Can we get the legal redlines from your team as a single track (Docx) so we can incorporate them into the DocuSign addendum?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention sunlight: clarification on backup purge and evidence handoff

Alex — quick operational notes from the backups team:

- Subprocessor: snapshots for Starlight are stored in Redwood-managed object storage within the same cloud region; we use an internal subprocessor process for lifecycle automation (no external third-party backup vendor for this customer).
- Default purge cadence: nightly GC with a 90-day tombstone window; purge jobs run in batches to avoid throughput spikes (we can provide the cron schedule).
- Exception workflow: customers request a temporary hold via Support (portal ticket -> ops on-call escalation). Ops will register a short-term retain token against the snapshot namespace; this token keeps the object alive beyond GC for a configured number of days (min 7 / max 180). Typical execution SLA: 24 hours to register a hold, 48–72 hours for ops to complete a scoped export request.

Evidence we can produce on request:
- Snapshot manifest (JSON) with object ids and checksums
- Purge job run logs (timestamps + affected object ids)
- Audit trace showing who requested the hold and the authorization ticket id

For Starlight specifically, I believe they asked for evidence usable for a forensics hold. We can produce a redacted sample manifest and an anonymized purge log to show the format; full evidence will be on a per-request basis.

Marissa — can you attach the runbook excerpt and the sample manifest so Alex has something to hand to legal? Vanessa, can you confirm storage region and whether cross-region replication affects the hold semantics?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: runbook-excerpt.md (internal), sample-snapshot-manifest.json (redacted)

Thanks — this is very helpful and close to what we need.

Procurement + Legal notes: the sample manifest and runbook excerpt look good. A couple of follow-ups before we sign:
1) DocuSign addendum: Legal wants a clause that guarantees a 48-hour maximum for registering emergency short-term holds for PII-bearing snapshots (you mentioned 24 hours to register; we need that as a hard SLA in the addendum). If Redwood can commit to 24 hours for registration and 72 hours for a scoped export delivery, that will work for us.
2) Cross-region replication: we need confirmation that replication copies are covered by the same hold token (Vanessa, please confirm).
3) Evidence retention: we ask that purge job logs and manifest checksums used as evidence are retained for 12 months post-purge for compliance audit. Is that feasible?

If you can confirm 1–3 and provide a DocuSign-ready addendum draft (we've attached our redlines: Starlight_DPA_redlines_v3.docx), procurement will prepare signature routing.

Thanks again — cc'ing procurement.

Alex Rivera
Data Operations Manager
Starlight Health
